verdict: The Cebu Marathon is one of the Philippines' original destination marathons — a January fixture that has drawn runners to Cebu City for years with a four-distance format (42K, 21K, 10K, 5K) and the promise of island recovery: beaches, lechon, and whale-shark watching a short drive away. The 2027 edition is listed for 10 January, though registration hasn't been confirmed yet, which is the main planning gap. The race has historically started in the pre-dawn hours, routing through Cebu City's central districts and across the Marcelo Fernan Bridge to Mactan Island — a course feature that gives the race its signature. Suits runners who want a Philippine destination marathon with established history; wait for registration to be confirmed before booking.

sections.heading: The Race: A Cebu City Institution
paragraphs: Organised by the dedicated Cebu Marathon team, this race has been a fixture on the Philippine calendar through multiple editions. [1] Four distances — full marathon (42.195km), half marathon (21.1km), 10km, and 5km — make it broad enough to attract serious marathoners and first-timers alike. The course historically crosses the Marcelo Fernan Bridge connecting Cebu City to Mactan Island, a signature feature that gives runners a bridge-crossing sunrise moment.

sections.heading: The Destination: Cebu City and Beyond
paragraphs: Cebu City is the Philippines' oldest city and its second-largest urban centre — a destination that combines urban running infrastructure with easy access to beaches, diving, and the famous Cebu lechon. For runners travelling in, Mactan-Cebu International Airport has direct flights from across Asia, and the city offers accommodation across every budget. The January date is dry-season in Cebu, with morning temperatures in the mid-20s Celsius.
